name: Bar Winkler
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Wonderful (enterprise AI agent platform)
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Wonderful in early 2025 with CTO Roey Lalazar to build AI agents for enterprise customer service, especially in non-English markets. Previously founded procurement startup Approve.com (sold to Tipalti, 2021). Wonderful raised $150M at a $2B valuation (2026 Series B) and then $550M at ~$5B (Sept 2026).
interesting_fact: Wonderful went from founding in early 2025 to a ~$5B valuation in under two years and ~650 employees across 35+ markets, deploying local teams alongside its AI agents.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Approve.com, Winkler was an early employee at ironSource, the Israeli app-monetization company that later went public at an ~$11B valuation.
notes: Hurun lists the industry as Agriculture, but this is Wonderful the Israeli AI company (wonderful.ai), not The Wonderful Company. Valuation is now ~$5B, not $2B. No personal press email found; use company channels.

name: Somanadri Bhupal
current_role: No current role found; former director of Aragen (formerly GVK Biosciences) and of GVK-group companies
profile: A GVK-group-linked director who served on the board of GVK Biosciences (now Aragen Life Sciences, Hyderabad CRO) until about 2009, and as a non-executive director of GVK Power & Infrastructure and Novopan Industries. Aragen itself was founded in 2001 by G V Sanjay Reddy; Hurun's 'founder' label for Bhupal appears to reflect a promoter-family stake rather than a founding role.
interesting_fact: Aragen began on 2 April 2001 as GVK BIO, an informatics company in Hyderabad, and was renamed Aragen Life Sciences in 2021; it is now one of India's larger contract research and manufacturing organisations.

Could not confirm current status or that he is a founder. The only route found is via Aragen or the GVK group.

name: Stefan Wawrzinek
current_role: Co-founder and managing director (Geschäftsführer), osapiens (Mannheim); described as COO/Chairman in third-party profiles
profile: German software entrepreneur who co-founded osapiens in Mannheim in 2018 with Alberto Zamora and Matthias Jungblut. osapiens sells a SaaS 'HUB' for supply-chain transparency, ESG/regulatory compliance (e.g. EUDR, CSRD) and carbon data, used by 2,500+ companies in 60+ countries. It became Germany's first unicorn of 2026 after a $100M round from BlackRock/Temasek-backed Decarbonization Partners.
interesting_fact: osapiens hit a $1B+ valuation in January 2026 with a $100M round led by Decarbonization Partners, the BlackRock-Temasek climate investment venture; Handelsblatt called it Germany's first unicorn of 2026.
deep_cut_fact: osapiens is a second act: Wawrzinek and his co-founders had previously worked in supply-chain monitoring and sold their first company to US conglomerate Honeywell before starting osapiens.
notes: Keeps a lower public profile than co-CEOs Zamora and Jungblut, who do most of the press. Sources disagree on his exact title (COO vs Chairman); the imprint confirms he is a managing director.

name: Oege de Moor
current_role: Founder & CEO, XBOW (autonomous AI penetration testing)
profile: Dutch-born computer scientist and former Oxford professor who spun out code-analysis company Semmle (CodeQL), acquired by GitHub in 2019; at GitHub he led the GitHub Next research group behind the original Copilot. He founded XBOW, whose AI agent autonomously finds and exploits security flaws, and which raised a $75M Series B and is valued at ~$1B per Hurun.
interesting_fact: In June 2025 XBOW became the first autonomous system to reach #1 on HackerOne's US bug-bounty leaderboard, outranking every human hacker.
deep_cut_fact: Before startups, de Moor was a functional-programming academic: with Jeremy Gibbons he co-edited 'The Fun of Programming' (Palgrave, 2003), and his Oxford CodeQuest research on querying code with Datalog became the basis of Semmle's QL/CodeQL.

public_contacts.value: https://xbow.com (contact/demo form on site; newsroom at https://xbow.com/newsroom)

notes: Hurun lists the industry as Aerospace, but XBOW is a cybersecurity/AI company. He writes on XBOW's blog and is active on X. The QuickCheck Wikipedia page cites the book he co-edited.
